subject.title: Bug: OAuth token exchange silently proceeds without client_secret + hardcoded redirect port

question: For Google/Gemini and Google Meet OAuth, should OpenClaw allow public-client PKCE token exchange without client_secret, warn on missing client_secret, or fail closed for configured confidential-client flows?
rationale: Current source and Google's native-app OAuth docs support optional secrets for some flows, but the issue raises a security boundary; automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Document and preserve public-client PKCE
options.body: Keep client_secret optional where Google public/native OAuth supports it, but add explicit docs or diagnostics so omission is intentional rather than silent.

options.title: Fail closed for configured confidential clients
options.body: Require client_secret only when the selected OAuth client type or plugin config declares a confidential/web-client flow, with tests for public-client compatibility.

options.title: Warn without changing behavior
options.body: Emit a clear setup warning when only client_id is configured, preserving current compatibility while surfacing the tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Document and preserve public-client PKCE
recommendation.body: Keep client_secret optional where Google public/native OAuth supports it, but add explicit docs or diagnostics so omission is intentional rather than silent.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining contract spans the Google provider OAuth path where commit metadata shows recent feature ownership.
